Import a fiber-bench receipt 11-07 → 11-05

In the separate 11-07 fiber bench, export a completed transfer. Choose that JSON here, or edit and apply a compatible receipt. Only connected synthetic output spectra within the teaching band, 440–500 nm, are supported. The input is never silently replaced when a draft is rejected.

How the meter calculates a reading Model & limits

One detector, two different quantities

Incident power is the area under the imported post-transfer spectrum S. The virtual photocurrent is ∫S(λ)R(λ)dλ; divide by R at the applied wavelength to obtain the indicated power. We integrate the product exactly between piecewise-linear samples. mW × A/W gives mA.

The response R(λ) = 0.25 + 0.005(λ − 470) A/W from 440–500 nm is an authored teaching curve, not Thorlabs calibration. We do not model detector noise, firmware, physical fiber loss, serial-specific calibration or optical hardware control. The 11-07 file hands off a virtual reference plane; it does not imply a physical connection between real instruments.

Try the example, then λ → ▲ → OK → Read. In this fixture the incident power remains 0.400 mW and the current remains 0.100 mA, while the indication falls from 0.400 mW at 470 nm to about 0.333 mW at 480 nm. A detached cable produces no reading; a valid, connected dark fixture produces a numerical zero.

Handbooks and reference photographs

  • Console face and sensor socket · Thorlabs PM100D Operation Manual, 17654-D02 Rev H (20 Sep 2017) · Printed p. 10 · Figs. 1–2. The left LCD, right navigation pad and lower direct keys identify the original PM100D. Its DB9 sensor input and electrical SMA analog output are separate.
  • Underside and back of the console · Thorlabs PM100D Operation Manual, 17654-D02 Rev H (20 Sep 2017) · Printed p. 11 · Figs. 3–4. The red protective boot surrounds the case. The rear support lifts away from the back; the SD slot and threaded mount are on the lower edge.
  • Wavelength selection · Thorlabs PM100D Operation Manual, 17654-D02 Rev H (20 Sep 2017) · Printed p. 18 · §4.2.3.2. The wavelength key opens a selection window. Arrows choose a stored wavelength and the center key confirms it. The actual console uses sensor calibration at that wavelength.
  • Console dimensions and side labels · Thorlabs PM100D Operation Manual, 17654-D02 Rev H (20 Sep 2017) · Printed p. 66 · §8.3. The booted console and visible LCD have catalog dimensions; the manual identifies the sensor and analog connectors on the left.
  • Exact sensor and housing dimensions · Thorlabs S120C Spec Sheet, 18356-S01 Rev C (4 Feb 2016) · PDF p. 2 · Specification table. The newer silicon S120C has a reflective ND filter. The catalog range and dimensions refer to the photodiode head, not the display. No second filter is applied in the teaching calculation.
  • S120C mechanical drawing and connector photo · Thorlabs S120C Spec Sheet, 18356-S01 Rev C (4 Feb 2016) · PDF p. 3 · Dimensions. The circular head carries its cable to a red male D-sub plug with release tabs. The central opening and externally threaded front are distinct.
  • S120-SMA engineering drawing · Thorlabs 14170-E01 Rev A (2006) · Sheet 1 of 1 · section A–A. The shallow circular cap has an internal SM1 fixing and a protruding SMA fitting; a central bore runs through the cap. The drawing is not a manufacturing specification.
  • Photograph of S120C with S120-SMA attached · Thorlabs PM100D product archive (21 Oct 2025) · PDF p. 5 · Fig. 5.2. Use the right-hand photograph. It shows the optical SMA adapter on the photodiode; the adjacent left figure is the physically different FC adapter. The post is a separate accessory.
  • Manufacturer archive record · Thorlabs PM100D product archive (21 Oct 2025) · Model overview and compatible sensors. Identifies the discontinued original PM100D. The illustrated working copy is provided separately; this model is not a PM100D2 or PM100D3.

Limits

  • No hardware measurements, serial calibration, absolute accuracy, noise floor, or physical-headset validation are claimed.
  • The response curve, spectrum, and indicated powers are synthetic. Documentation establishes controls, interfaces and nominal geometry only.
  • Wear, key travel, cable curves, grip and bore details, unreported component placements, and optional support geometry are visual approximations. No tolerance-stack or physical coupling/loss claim.
  • The 2016 S120C sheet depicts the later reflective-filter head. Older S120C filter constructions are not portrayed. The reference photos do not document the exact virtual specimen or the entire virtual assembly together.
